name: Back extension and good morning
pattern: Trunk and hip extension: the trunk lowers forward from the hips and lifts back to a straight line, with the legs fixed.
setup: Set the pad just below the hip crease so the hips can bend freely.
Heels against the foot plate, legs straight or a little soft.
Arms crossed on the chest; harder: hands by the head or a plate on the chest.

steps.text: Bend at the hips and lower the trunk under control.
Stop when you feel the hamstrings stretch or the back starts to round.
Squeeze glutes and lift the trunk back up.
Stop in a straight line from head to heels. Do not arch past it.

cues.cue: Finish in a straight line, not an arch.
cues.why: Over-arching adds load on the lumbar joints without extra hip work.

cues.cue: Hinge at the hips; pad below the hip crease.
cues.why: The 45° back extension works glutes and hamstrings strongly as well as the back.

cues.cue: Make it harder by moving the arms up: chest, head, then overhead.
cues.why: Back muscle activity rose step by step with hand position and a more horizontal bench.

cues.cue: To target the back, bend the hips less and move the spine more.
cues.why: Limiting hip flexion cut hamstring activity and kept the load on the back extensors.

cues.cue: Smooth reps, no bouncing at the bottom.
cues.why: Momentum takes load off the muscles you are training.

breathing: Breathe in going down, out as you lift.

mistakes.name: Over-arching at the top
mistakes.looks: The chest lifts above the line of the legs and the low back pinches.
mistakes.fix: Stop when your body is straight; squeeze glutes.
mistakes.why: Range at the top comes from lumbar extension only.

mistakes.name: Bouncing out of the bottom
mistakes.looks: The trunk drops fast and rebounds up.
mistakes.fix: Two seconds down, a short pause, then lift.
mistakes.why: The stretch reflex and momentum do the work.

mistakes.name: Back rounds under load (good morning)
mistakes.looks: The upper and low back curve as you bend forward with the bar.
mistakes.fix: Lighter load, soft knees, stop higher.
mistakes.why: A loaded flexed spine is the riskiest version of the hinge.

safety: Low back pain: start on the floor or with a short range; avoid loaded good mornings until pain-free.
Good morning: start light; knees bend more as the load goes up.

variants.change: Load held at the chest or behind the neck; hold it close.
Rotate the trunk at the top: more oblique work.
One foot on the plate: more glute and hamstring on that side.
Spine curls down and up on purpose with the hips fixed: targets the back muscles; keep the load light.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top for upper back work.
Over a stability ball, feet against a wall: smaller range, easier.
Hold the straight-body position for time.
Seated machine: less glute and hamstring work than the 45° bench.
Standing with a bar on the back; knees almost straight; no knee flexion moment, so hamstrings carry the hip work.
Trunk fixed, legs swing up behind you; posterior chain work without spinal load from above.

subtypes.name: 90° back extension
subtypes.change: Body horizontal at the top; trunk lowers toward vertical.

subtypes.name: Good morning
subtypes.change: Standing, bar on the upper back, knees soft, hinge until the trunk is near level.

subtypes.name: Reverse hyperextension
subtypes.match: reverse hyper|reverse back extension|reverse extension|reverse hyperextension
subtypes.change: Trunk on the pad, hips at the edge; legs swing from hanging down up to straight behind you.

subtypes.name: Floor back extension
subtypes.match: floor hyperextension|lying back extension|lying floor|lower back curl|snow angel|lying hyperextension|static position lying front
subtypes.change: Lying face down, lift the chest a little off the floor.

motion.basis: 45° Roman chair default: at the top the body is a straight line tilted 45°, so trunk = 45 + hip flexion. Good morning knee about 5° from schellenberg2013, rising with load in vigotsky2015; reverse hyper hip and trunk flex about 5° more with heavy loads (lawrence2022). Other angles are estimates.
